Maria: quick flag - I'm seeing a reproducible KV cache memory climb on on-prem during long-context regen-load. Dedicated/Hosted look stable but onprem nodes show steady pages_in_use growth and periodic msync spikes.
Maria: repro and minimal artifacts below. started cold, regen-load 100 concurrent sessions, 25k context, ~30m run, captured kv_dump + perf.
Maria: ```
./regen-load --model redwood-v2q --kv-mode=shared --context=25000 --concurrency=100 --duration=30m
sleep 60 && ./kv_dump --top=80 > /tmp/kv-dump.onprem.log
perf record -F 99 -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 120
```
Raj: can try on a dedicated dev node today. any quick kv_dump snippet you can paste here?
Maria: small kv dump excerpt: 
```
entries: 482900
pages_in_use: 6020 -> 7891 (+31%)
avg_slot_kv_size: 5.0KB
holes>64B: 11.8%
```
Linh: interesting. on Hosted/Dedicated have jemalloc tuned (MALLOC_CONF) and newer kernels. onprem is distro malloc + older kernel. allocator/gpu driver/kernel combos often explain physical fragmentation.
Tony: don't forget RDMA/CUDA pinning. Onprem uses RoCE in that rack and we had past issues where RDMA registrations prevent pages from being reclaimed which shows up as msync/madvise/long-lived pinned pages.
Maria: onprem → kernel 5.4 / nvidia 470.82 / CUDA 11.0. Dedicated → kernel 5.15 / 525.x. Hosted → kernel 6.x / 535.x.
Raj: big delta. jemalloc + MALLOC_CONF tweaks we use reduce small-allocation churn. Can we try LD_PRELOAD jemalloc on onprem as a quick experiment?
Jamie: proposed quick mitigation experiment (low blast radius): LD_PRELOAD jemalloc + force 4K slab alignment and small-page runtime kernel. steps:
```
LD_PRELOAD=/opt/thirdparty/jemalloc/lib/libjemalloc.so \
MALLOC_CONF=\"narenas:1,lg_dirty_mult:32,background_thread:true\" \
KV_SLAB_ALIGN=4096 \
KV_FORCE_SMALLPAGES=1 \
./service restart
# then run regen-load same as above
```
Linh: additionally collect /proc/<pid>/smaps series, pmap -x snapshots every 2m and `cat /proc/<pid>/numa_maps`. We need to confirm whether fragmentation is virtual (vma holes) vs physical (resident pages).
Maria: perf snippet: noted msync spikes roughly every 45-60s aligned with our KV eviction sweep. msync -> __do_sys_msync and madvise MADV_DONTNEED are top kernel symbols.
Tony: suggest checking `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` and RDMA registration stats during run. Also `cat /sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-2048kB/nr_hugepages` and `grep HUGETLB /boot/config-$(uname -r)` to see hugepage behavior. mixing huge and small pages can fragment slab backing.
Raj: I'll reproduce on a dedicated dev node and run two variants: (A) match onprem driver/kernel if dev infra allows, (B) dedicated with smallpage kernel. I'll collect perf.data + kv_dumps and upload.
Maria: infra-bot created INF-4829: "kv cache fragmentation repro on onprem (driver/allocator/rdma suspect)" https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-4829
Jamie: additional quick config leverage: bumping max_batch_age from 5ms -> 12ms reduced allocation churn in short synthetic runs. It's a plausible stopgap to reduce insert/evict rates at cost of small tail latency. Worth A/B.
Linh: good idea. please capture allocation hotspots with pprof (allocs) and also jemalloc stats if we enable it via LD_PRELOAD. That will tell us if churn comes from batching path.
Maria: action items:
- Raj: run dedicated comparisons and upload artifacts (perf.data + kv_dumps + smaps) to S3: s3://redwood-internal/tmp/kvfrag/1943216789/
- Jamie: build jemalloc LD_PRELOAD binary and runbook for onprem (EOD)
- Linh: collect kernel config, hugepage state, numa_maps across envs
- Tony: test RDMA pinning hypothesis with infra (disable RoCE on a test rack) and gather `dmesg | grep -i dma` / `ibv_devinfo` output
- Maria: attach current perf artifacts to INF-4829 and coordinate A/B plan
infra-bot: INF-4829 updated with initial artifacts and action items -> https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-4829 :white_check_mark:
Raj: I'll try smallpage kernel + jemalloc LD_PRELOAD and report numbers by EOD. if the growth stops with jemalloc, we likely have allocator fragmentation causing elevated physical RSS.
Maria: if short-term mitigations (jemalloc preload + KV_SLAB_ALIGN OR bump max_batch_age) look good, we can roll a runtime override for onprem pools while root cause is investigated.
Jamie: scheduling A/B: 50% onprem pool gets jemalloc preload + batch_age bump, 50% baseline. collect 6h telemetry and compare pages_in_use curves.
Linh: note: also ensure no periodic userland process triggers msync (backup/scan). check crontabs and any monitoring agents.
Maria: thanks all, uploading perf + dumps now to the ticket and will ping when complete.
